headline: Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Spot gold edges higher as oil prices tumble after Trump delays fresh Iran strike
body: Gold prices remained in focus after spot gold rose 0.4% and US gold futures gained 0.9% as oil prices tumbled on expectations of fresh US-Iran talks.
full_body:
Rupee surged 31 paise to 95.12 against the US dollar in early trade on Monday over a steep fall in global crude oil prices and a softer greenback after US President Donald Trump decided to hold off strikes against Iran.

FII inflows, a rise in the country's forex reserves, and Reserve Bank of India (RBI) support further strengthened the local unit, according to forex traders.

At the interbank foreign exchange, the rupee opened at 95.15 against the greenback before rising further to 95.12, up 31 paise from its previous close.

Gold prices rose in early trade on Monday as crude oil prices slumped after US President Donald Trump held off on fresh military action against Iran, raising hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough and easing concerns over inflation and higher interest rates.

Spot gold gained 0.4% to $4,055.76 an ounce, while US gold futures climbed 0.9% to $4,054.00.

The US dollar also weakened after authorities intervened in the foreign exchange market to support the Japanese yen, making dollar-denominated gold cheaper for overseas buyers.

Trump said talks with Iran would take place on Monday but declined to set a deadline for reaching an agreement. The prospect of negotiations pushed oil prices down by more than 5%, easing fears of a prolonged supply disruption.

Gold has remained under pressure since the outbreak of the US-Iran conflict, as higher oil prices could fuel inflation and prompt central banks to keep interest rates elevated.

Google has taken down a day-old feature that allowed users of Google Earth to generate AI images, with the rollback coming after people online shared deepfake images of terrorist attacks and other forms of destruction.

The feature had allowed users of Google Earth to build on the available imagery and generate AI images using it, via text prompts. Introduced earlier this week on July 30, it was taken down after a day or so, following reports of people misusing it, as well as customer criticism.

The AI image generation feature was powered by Google’s Nano Banana 2 AI model, which enjoyed viral popularity at the time of its initial launch and sparked multiple AI-image trends.

While Google did not provide examples of the AI-generated content that violated its policies, screenshots on Elon Musk-owned X showed realistic satellite images featuring false terror attacks, industrial accidents, and other forms of violence.

Some Google users expressed concerns that the technology could be used to spread propaganda or false news about the impact of ongoing conflicts and environmental disasters.

“We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world. We’ve seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes, however we’ve also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies. So we’re rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails,” posted Google on X on July 31.

headline: What ‘Pacing the Frontier’ reveals about the U.S. AI industry | Explained
body: The U.S. AI industry boasts of a short yet rich tradition of open letters signed by tech companies, but do these efforts lead to any meaningful results?
full_body:

The story so far: In late July, 1,319 employees working at some of the world’s frontier AI companies signed and released an open letter titled ‘Pacing the Frontier.’ In it, they called on the U.S. government to help address the lack of technical and governance tools to regulate the speed at which frontier-wide progress was taking place. Those who signed included senior executives and department chiefs from AI firms including Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and more.

In under 200 words, the 1,319 tech workers and leaders outlined the potential of AI to change the world, and said that there were signs of automated AI research becoming a reality soon. They warned that the world “may need the option to buy time” in order to better understand and control these emerging systems. However, the letter admitted that the pressure of ongoing competition between AI companies, as well as countries, made it difficult to slow down.

“We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development,” stated the letter’s call to action.

Along with this statement, a number of individual signatories contributed their personal comments and warnings about advancing AI systems.

While not officially stated, it was understood that the incident triggering the release of the letter was a cybersecurity breach from two weeks earlier. This was when a combination of OpenAI’s models broke out of their internal testing environment and breached the infrastructure of AI firm Hugging Face , purportedly to source the solutions they needed. On July 28, OpenAI stated that its models identified and used publicly exposed credentials for multiple accounts on at least four services.

On July 30, Anthropic came forward to disclose three cybersecurity incidents, saying that its Claude model reached the internet via a third-party evaluation environment, and then “gained unauthorized access” to the systems of three organisations.

headline: Diesel’s desire: an engine for everyone
body: For someone who wished to build an engine for everyone, August turned out to be an auspicious month. On August 10, 1893, Rudolf Diesel’s prime model was powered on its own for the first time. Five years later, on August 9, 1898, Diesel obtained a U.S. patent titled “Internal-combustion engine”. Join A.S.Ganesh as he tries to explain what fuelled Diesel’s desire…
full_body:

What are your motivations? Barring what we do spontaneously, almost all of our actions are driven by motivations. It is, in fact, all-encompasing, starting from the seemingly mundane to those that define us as a being.

In case you are wondering how, think about this. We brush and bathe for our own wellbeing. We behave a certain way with our friends and family members, motivated by our own perception of ourselves. We study and work to fulfil our own goals, objectives, and ambitions. You get the drift.

Be it the one sitting next to you as you are reading this, or the one who is looking to run for a country’s highest office in the future, everyone has their own motivations to do what they do. The scientists and inventors, whom we often place on a pedestal after their accomplishments, aren’t too different.

Even in the case of serendipitous inventions and discoveries, the ones working on it have put themselves in a position to notice what is panning out through a lifetime of conditioning to spot those very things. And then, there are those who spend a lifetime towards a goal, without certainty as to whether it will ever be realised or not. French-born German engineer and inventor Rudolf Diesel neatly fits into the second category.

Now best remembered for the engine that bears his name, Diesel was much more than just an inventor. He dabbled with languages, admired the arts, and was also a social theorist who tried to study and understand existing social phenomena.

In fact, his concept of sociological needs was one of his prime motivators as an inventor. That, along with creative mechanical designs and a thorough understanding of heat transference by natural physical processes or laws, were the three underlying commonalities in most of Diesel’s inventions.
